_status: Module 3, Lesson 3.2 'Keys: the part people forget' (learner guide of 21 October 2026): who holds the key, where it is kept, who can recover it, when it changes. Cases invented around the fictional RSSO; case 4 follows the guide's Try it 3.2 model answer 7.

items.text: Ana keeps the nightly backup's encryption key in a text file on the same backup drive.

facts.v: Apart from the data it protects, never on the same drive or server

items.reason: Whoever steals both can read everything.

items.text: The database key is held by Ana, with a backup custodian, and a sealed recovery copy that Director Eva approved.

facts.v: A named key custodian, for example Ana, with a backup custodian
Through a sealed recovery procedure approved by the head of office

items.reason: The office can open its own data even when Ana is away.

items.text: Ana's assistant, who knew where the backup key is kept, leaves the RSSO. Nothing changes.

facts.v: On a schedule, and at once when a custodian leaves or a key may be exposed

items.reason: A key someone outside the office may know is no longer secret.

items.text: Dan emails the encrypted payout file to the e-wallet provider, with its password in the same email.

facts.v: Use the provider's business portal over HTTPS instead of email; if email cannot be avoided, an encrypted file with the password sent another way

items.reason: A password that travels with the file opens it for anyone who intercepts the email.

items.text: Only Ana knows the key to the encrypted database. There is no recovery procedure.

facts.v: Through a sealed recovery procedure approved by the head of office

items.reason: One absence, or one lost key, locks the office out of its own data: Ready is hit.
